newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Russia approve first-phase anti-missile pact.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Russia approve first-phase anti-missile pact.

text.p: The United States and Russia on Monday approved the first phase of a new agreement on anti- missile systems and called for negotiations on the second phase to start next month.

U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said after talks with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov the two sides had reached a milestone in their attempt to work out which systems will be permitted under a 24-year-old arms treaty.

U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin last year asked negotiators to work out which systems were strategic, and hence limited by the 1972 Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty, and which were smaller-scale "theater" systems which are not limited.

Experts from the United States, Russia, Kazakhstan, Belarus and Ukraine worked out a draft accord in June on lower-speed systems. "What we did today was to confirm that the United States and Russia accept those documents ... and are prepared now to move ahead as quickly as possible to complete the final agreement," Under Secretary of State Lynn Davis said.

The phase one agreement specifies that all theater missile defense systems with interceptor speeds up to three km per second (1.8 miles per second) are permitted under the ABM treaty, unless they are tested against targets with speeds over five km per second (3.1 miles per second) or ranges greater than 3,500 km (2,174 miles), she told reporters.

Primakov said at a joint news conference with Christopher he believed the accord would have a "positive effect" on prospects for Russia's parliament ratifying the START-2 U.S.-Russian strategic missile treaty.
